newsitem.title: INDIA: India's communists see new government next week.
newsitem.headline: India's communists see new government next week.

text.p: India's two main communist parties, heading an influential leftwing bloc in the ousted United Front coalition, said on Tuesday they were confident a new government would be formed by next week.

"A new government will be formed soon," a senior leader of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) told Reuters. Asked if the government would be in place before a special budget session of parliament begins on April 21, he said: "It could be one or two days beyond that."
An official of the Communist Party of India (CPI) said the Left Front would discuss the bloc's strategy at a meeting on Wednesday.
"We are of course clear that a new government has to be put in place to fight the threat to secularism," the official said.

Both parties said they would join a meeting of the United Front's decision-making Steering Committe on Thursday when a new leader is expected to be named to succeed caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
The new leader was to be formally endorsed by a meeting of the United Front's deputies scheduled for Sunday, a day before parliament meets to discuss the budget, the CPI official said.
